s1.syndrome_frame: Widespread skin condition with progressive worsening and characteristic plaques
salient_findings: Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale
key_facts: The patient is a 32-year-old woman
The skin condition has progressively worsened
The condition involves 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques are present on the trunk and extremities
The plaques involve 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs are sparse and less than 5 mm long
Scalp hairs are coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic erythematous plaques and progressive worsening

shortlist.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Erythroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of 90% of body surface area and widespread skin condition

shortlist.label: Psoriatic erythroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of psoriasis and erythroderma symptoms

shortlist.label: Generalized pustular psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe skin condition with potential for pustular lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques, involvement of 90% of her body surface area, and skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis are consistent with psoriatic erythroderma. The presence of coarse and brittle scalp hairs and sparse eyebrow hairs also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: While it can cause erythematous plaques, the absence of characteristic palmoplantar keratoderma and the presence of psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia make it less likely

rejected.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
rejected.why: The extent of body surface area involvement (90%) and the presence of erythroderma are not typical of psoriasis vulgaris

rejected.label: Erythroderma
rejected.why: Erythroderma is a more general term that can be caused by various conditions, including psoriasis. The specific findings in this case, such as psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, point towards a more specific diagnosis of psoriatic erythroderma

rejected.label: Generalized pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: The absence of pustules in the description and the presence of serpiginous, erythematous plaques make this diagnosis less likely
